intro.title: Discover the Square
intro.description: Piazza del Popolo is the beating heart of Ascoli Piceno, one of the most elegant squares in Italy. Entirely paved in travertine, it is surrounded by Renaissance buildings with harmonious porticoes.
highlights: Entirely clad in local travertine stone
Palazzo dei Capitani del Popolo (13th century)
Historic Caffè Meletti, an Art Nouveau gem

visitDuration.title: How long does a visit take?
visitDuration.text: A visit to the square takes about 1-2 hours. Allow extra time for a coffee at Meletti and to explore the surrounding streets of the historic centre.

worthIt.title: Is it worth visiting?
worthIt.text: Look at Palazzo dei Capitani del Popolo and its civic presence, then the Gothic forms of San Francesco and the adjacent Loggia dei Mercanti. Finish at the façade of Caffè Meletti. Compare the different architectural details instead of treating every building as Renaissance. Entering a café means checking its current service and prices.

getting-here.title: Getting to Piazza del Popolo
getting-here.intro: Arrive on foot in the historic centre
sections: Arrive on foot in the historic centre

The square is in the historic centre of Ascoli Piceno. Use Piazza del Popolo, 63100 Ascoli Piceno AP as your destination; do not confuse it with squares of the same name in other Italian cities. The final approach is best planned as a walk, rather than a drive to the square itself.

The municipality regulates pedestrian areas and restricted vehicle access. A navigation route is not permission to enter. Before driving into the centre, consult the municipal rules and signs for your vehicle and travel date. Choose a permitted parking location and check its operator for current access, charges and opening hours; this guide does not promise a space or a fare.

Check your rail or bus operator for the date of travel, then plan the last part to Piazza del Popolo separately. Do not treat the square as the railway station or a vehicle drop-off point. Allow extra time for luggage and ask your accommodation about an authorised drop-off if needed.

walking-route.title: A self-guided walk around the square
walking-route.intro: A flexible route, without a timed ticket
sections: A flexible route, without a timed ticket

Start in the open square and look across the travertine paving before approaching the façades. Walk along the porticoes, keeping shop entrances and pedestrian routes clear. This is a suggested outdoor circuit, not a measured accessible route or a promise that every passage is open.

Look at Palazzo dei Capitani del Popolo and its civic presence, then the Gothic forms of San Francesco and the adjacent Loggia dei Mercanti. Finish at the façade of Caffè Meletti. Compare the different architectural details instead of treating every building as Renaissance. Entering a café means checking its current service and prices.

buildings-and-opening.intro: The square and the interiors have different rules
sections: The square and the interiors have different rules

Seeing a building from Piazza del Popolo does not establish access to its rooms, roof or tower. The outdoor square, religious services, exhibitions and commercial premises each have their own arrangements. Check the relevant operator before making an interior visit the main purpose of a journey.
Palazzo dei Capitani: check before entering

An official reconstruction notice dated 24 July 2026 reports works on Palazzo dei Capitani. It does not provide a verified completion date for this guide. Do not infer that all interiors are open from the public access to the square; confirm the current programme, affected areas and any admission arrangements with the municipality.
